title: The seven articles of the U.S. Constitution
trouble: Rereading feels like knowing; it is not. Recall, then check.

blocks.html: The Constitution has only seven articles, and each has one job. Once you know which article does what, the whole document has a map: the three branches first, then the states, then how to change it, how it stands above other laws, and how it came into force.

How to hold it: Seven things fit in a short list, so learn all seven as one chunk. A first-letter sentence helps hold the order: Lively Eagles Jump Over Steep Stony Ridges, for Legislative, Executive, Judicial, the States, Amendments (changing it), Supreme law, Ratification. Then build pictures on a memory palace route: a busy hall of lawmakers at the front door, a desk with a presidential seal in the hall, a judge's gavel on the stairs, fifty state flags in the kitchen, a pencil and eraser in the dining room, a crown on the top shelf, and nine signatures on the back door. Recall it by walking the route, and come back on day 1, 3, 7 and 21.
